watch.subject: LUCK and ILP: qualify the growth core
watch.trigger: Investigate LUCK and ILP first because their screens report positive EPS growth. Require recurring consolidated earnings growth, cash conversion, attractive reinvestment, sponsor delivery and minority treatment, and a balance sheet that survives higher rates. Satisfactory business evidence triggers rebuilding toward the 75% core default without waiting for a price rebound or a favorable event backtest. Determine final names and weights from that evidence; these are research candidates today.

Neither condition substitutes for qualifying the core businesses. The bundle does not establish the next MPC date.

exposure_reason: Choose 15% tactical exposure and 85% cash after explicitly weighing the approximately 75% core default. The decisive reason for withholding core capital is that this bundle does not establish normalized earnings, reinvestment returns, builder culture, sponsor delivery or balance-sheet resilience for a qualifying growth business. It supplies research candidates, not enough business evidence for me to underwrite a concentrated core. The relevant requirements are questions.md: "B1. What is five-year earnings power on consolidated EPS, one-offs stripped?", "B3. What does the business earn on new capital, and how much does it reinvest?", "B4. Is the business trying to become big, with a builder culture?", "B5. Who runs it, and did past promises meet delivery and past bets pay?", and "B7. Can the balance sheet survive higher rates and a bad year?". I accept the opportunity cost of this evidence threshold and would restore core exposure when those answers qualify the businesses, without requiring a bullish market signal. Weak timing evidence and price drawdowns do not by themselves justify abandoning the core: BRIEF says "the core rests on business questions, not on timing base rates." ATRL earns only a speculative allocation from the policy process and confirming price cited in entries[0]. At the specified entry and initial stop, 15 * (1219.1 - 975.28) / 1219.1 = 3% planned book risk, satisfying both entry-risk caps; this is planned stop risk, not a guaranteed loss ceiling.
not_known: Unverified: normalized earnings, reinvestment, sponsor delivery, debt and cash quality (questions.md B1/B3/B5/B7/B8); ATRL implementation economics (actors.md: "Approval is not implementation."); external accounts (market.md: "FX reserves, current account: not available in this repository (no data file)"); actual meeting dates (calendar.md); execution costs and fills. These gaps prevent a qualified core thesis and calibrated net-return probabilities.
